name: Bob Lee
category: Software engineer / fintech CTO (Cash App, Square)
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Google as a staff software engineer in October 2004 at age 24, contributing to Android and core Java libraries; by age 26 co-created the Guice dependency-injection framework (2006).
early_history_summary: Born in St. Louis, Missouri, Lee coded a 3D rendering engine in Turbo Pascal while at Lindbergh High School and attended Southeast Missouri State University. In 2001 he released a free Code Red worm defense tool, then worked as a technical architect at AT&T developing the dynaop AOP framework before Google recruited him in 2004.
family_context_summary: Raised in the St. Louis area; brother Tim Oliver Lee. Family financial status and parental occupations not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early programming, Google Android, Guice, open source Java
evidence_summary: Lee demonstrated deep systems programming skill from high school through AT&T and open-source work before Google hired him at 24 onto Android and core libraries. Co-authoring Guice with Kevin Bourrillion by 2006 and later winning a Jolt Award cemented scarce Java framework expertise. Moving to Square as CTO and helping create Cash App were later compounding steps on that technical base. Family background and early capital are not documented; advantages center on self-built technical depth and elite employer embedding.
starting_point: Born December 20, 1979 in St. Louis, Missouri; attended Lindbergh High School and Southeast Missouri State University.
current_position: Died April 4, 2023 at age 43 after a stabbing in San Francisco; final roles included Square CTO and MobileCoin chief product officer; known for co-creating Cash App.

trajectory.event: Released a free tool to defend Microsoft IIS servers against the Code Red worm.
Joined Google as staff software engineer working on Android and core Java libraries.
Co-created the Guice dependency-injection framework with Kevin Bourrillion at Google.
Received a Jolt Award for Guice; later joined expert groups on Java lambdas and concurrency.
Joined Square as CTO and led Android and later iOS product engineering.
Helped build Square Cash (later Cash App), a peer-to-peer payments product that became a major consumer fintech app.
Joined MobileCoin as chief product officer.
Fatally stabbed in San Francisco; Nima Momeni later convicted of second-degree murder.

name: Willem van Biljon
milestone_by_age_26: No material career-defining milestone by age 26 found; early research papers (1987–88) and junior research posts predate fame. Major achievements—co-founding Mosaic Software, leading Amazon EC2 product, and founding Nimbula—occurred in his 30s–40s.
early_history_summary: Born in Pretoria, South Africa in 1961, van Biljon graduated in computer science from the University of Cape Town and held engineering and research roles at LinkData, the Institute for Applied Computer Science, and the National Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences, publishing GIS and systems papers around ages 25–26.
evidence_summary: Van Biljon's public reputation rests on co-leading Amazon EC2 product management (mid-2000s, mid-40s) and co-founding Nimbula (sold to Oracle 2013). Pre-26 activity is ordinary academic research and early CS employment in South Africa, not a dated breakout founding or product milestone.

name: Katherine Johnson
milestone_by_age_26: Graduated summa cum laude from West Virginia State College in 1937 at age 18 with degrees in mathematics and French; by age 21 (1939) became the first African-American woman to enroll in graduate mathematics at West Virginia University after desegregation of its graduate school.
early_history_summary: Born Creola Katherine Coleman in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia, she showed exceptional math ability early, entered high school at age 10 because local schools stopped at eighth grade for Black students, graduated high school at 14, and completed dual bachelor's degrees at 18 under mentors including W. W. Schieffelin Claytor.
family_context_summary: Youngest of four children; mother Joylette was a teacher and father Joshua was a lumberman, farmer, handyman, and Greenbrier Hotel worker. Family rearranged life so children could attend high school on the WV State campus.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a teacher, supporting educational ambition; father worked multiple manual and service jobs rather than STEM/professional math roles.
primary_early_advantage_tags: math prodigy, HBCU mentors, segregation adversity, teacher mother
evidence_summary: Johnson's extreme early math ability—high school at 10, college at 14–18, dual degrees summa cum laude—was the primary engine, amplified by mentors Angie Turner King and Claytor who created advanced courses for her. Family support for education under Jim Crow constraints was real but financially modest. Later NACA/NASA trajectory work (from age 34) rode the space race, but the age-26-eligible record is the prodigy academic path and historic graduate-school integration.
starting_point: Born August 26, 1918 in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia, to a teacher mother and lumberman/farmer father in a segregated Jim Crow South.
current_position: Died February 24, 2020 at age 101 in Newport News, Virginia; celebrated NASA mathematician, Presidential Medal of Freedom (2015) and Congressional Gold Medal (2019) recipient.

trajectory.event: Graduated from high school on the West Virginia State College campus after entering high school at age 10.
Graduated summa cum laude from West Virginia State with degrees in mathematics and French.
Became the first African-American woman to attend graduate school at West Virginia University after desegregation of its graduate program.
Joined NACA Langley as a human computer in the West Area Computing unit.
Calculated trajectory and launch windows for Alan Shepard's Freedom 7 flight, the first American in space.
Personally verified electronic computer orbital calculations for John Glenn's Friendship 7 flight at his request.
Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Barack Obama.
Died in Newport News, Virginia, widely recognized as a pioneering NASA mathematician.

name: Ezra Callahan
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Facebook in December 2004 at about age 23 as one of the first ~20 employees and the company's first product manager, hired by Sean Parker during the Los Altos house era.
early_history_summary: Pasadena-area Polytechnic School class of 1999; graduated Stanford University Symbolic Systems in 2003. Briefly worked as business manager of the Stanford Daily before roommate/network ties to Sean Parker led to a 2004 Facebook hire; stayed through hypergrowth until ~2010.
family_context_summary: Not documented in detail in reviewed sources; attended private Polytechnic School in Pasadena, suggesting middle-to-upper-middle-class educational access.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford, Sean Parker, early Facebook, Silicon Valley
evidence_summary: Callahan's breakout was network-driven: Stanford Symbolic Systems, proximity to Sean Parker, and joining Facebook's tiny founding cohort in late 2004. He was not a technical cofounder but rode extreme structural upside as early PM/internal comms lead through 2010, later converting equity into hospitality and family-foundation work. Exact birth year is inferred from HS '99 and Stanford '03 (~1981); age at hire ~23 is consistent across sources.
starting_point: Raised in the Pasadena, California area; graduated Polytechnic School (1999) and Stanford Symbolic Systems (2003).
current_position: Runs the Callahan Family Foundation with wife Marisa; former early Facebook employee and hospitality entrepreneur (Arrive Hotels sold to Palisociety); resides in Southern California area.

trajectory.event: Graduated Stanford University with a Symbolic Systems degree.
Joined Facebook as one of the first employees and first product manager, hired by Sean Parker.
Left Facebook after roughly six years spanning product and internal communications roles.
Transitioned into hospitality entrepreneurship, later co-founding Arrive Hotels & Restaurants.
Purchased a large Pasadena mansion; continued family foundation and local civic engagement work.

name: James Bidzos
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Bidzos joined RSA Data Security as a leader in February 1986 at about age 30–31 and founded Verisign in 1995 at about age 40; early IBM career in the 1970s is not documented as a dated breakout achievement by 26.
early_history_summary: Born in 1955 in Greece and immigrated to the U.S. as a child; parents worked in service roles (father barber, mother restaurant manager per secondary profiles). Career prominence begins with turning around RSA from 1986 and later founding Verisign.
family_context_summary: Greek immigrant family; parents worked in service occupations after coming to the U.S. Detailed early finances not strongly documented in primary sources reviewed.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not documented as technology or cryptography professionals.
evidence_summary: Bidzos is a major internet security figure via RSA and Verisign, but those leadership milestones occur after age 30. Sources do not establish a specific material achievement at or before age 26.

name: Tom Gruber
milestone_by_age_26: No material career-defining milestone by age 26 found. Earned BS (1981) and MS (1984) by age 25 and completed a PhD in 1988 at about age 29; foundational ontology papers and Siri co-founding (2007) came well after age 26.
early_history_summary: Studied psychology and computer science at Loyola University New Orleans (BS 1981 summa cum laude), built an early CAI system, then MS (1984) and PhD (1988) at UMass Amherst on knowledge acquisition and communication prosthesis research.
evidence_summary: Gruber became widely known for ontology engineering in the 1990s and as Siri co-founder/CTO (2007–2010, Apple acquisition). Graduate degrees by mid-20s are solid but not a distinctive public milestone comparable to his later work; PhD and Stanford KSL period start after 26.

name: Steve Lee
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year found in reviewed sources; cannot verify age at Google product director roles, Bitcoin Optech contributions, or Square Crypto/Spiral leadership (public from ~2019). Without a birth year, a material milestone by age 26 cannot be established.
early_history_summary: Former Google product director who volunteered on Bitcoin Optech; hired by Square in 2019 as first member of its crypto team (later Square Crypto / Spiral) to support open-source Bitcoin and Lightning development. Co-founded Presidio Bitcoin activities in later coverage.
evidence_summary: Steve Lee (@moneyball) is a known Bitcoin open-source funder/product lead via Square Crypto/Spiral, but public profiles and interviews do not state birth year or age. Eligibility cannot be coded without that date.

name: John Britton
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 firmly established. Approximate birth ~1986–87 (stated age 38 in a May 2025 interview). Joined GitHub in 2012 (~age 25) but the flagship GitHub Student Developer Pack launched October 2014 (~age 27–28). Later co-founded Workbrew.
early_history_summary: Studied computer science at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (c. 2004–2009), worked in developer evangelism (including Twilio), then spent 2012–2019 at GitHub building Education programs including the Student Developer Pack and Campus Experts. Co-founder/CEO of Workbrew afterward.
evidence_summary: Britton is best known for GitHub Education and the Student Developer Pack, launched in 2014 when he was likely already past 26. Joining GitHub alone is not coded as a material age-26 milestone. Birth year is approximate from a 2025 age statement.

name: Deborah Washington Brown
milestone_by_age_26: Distinctive material milestone—first Black woman to earn a Harvard applied mathematics/computer science Ph.D. (1981)—occurred at age 28–29. By age 26 she had a Lowell Tech math BS (1975) and Harvard MS (1977) and was a PhD student, which is strong but not coded as the career-defining public milestone.
early_history_summary: Born June 3, 1952 in Washington, D.C.; National Cathedral School, brief New England Conservatory piano study, then math BS with honors at Lowell Technological Institute (1975) and Harvard applied math MS (1977)/PhD (1981). Later speech recognition work at Bell Labs with multiple patents.
family_context_summary: Youngest of four; mother Lola a hairdresser, father Edwin a taxi driver; parents encouraged education despite modest means.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not computer scientists; mother service/hair, father taxi driving.
evidence_summary: Brown's historic Harvard PhD in 1981 at ~29 is the clear material milestone in sources; industrial speech-recognition patents and Bell Labs career came later. Conservatively excluded for age-26 eligibility because the defining achievement is after 26.

name: Molly Graham
category: Tech operator / people & culture leader (Facebook, Quip, CZI)
milestone_by_age_26: Exact birth year not confirmed in reviewed sources. Joined Google comms (~2007) then Facebook (~2008) and was described as age 25 while in Facebook HR before a mobile product rotation; later COO roles at Quip and CZI and founding Glue Club are the clearer public achievements and appear post-26 or undated relative to a verified birth year. Conservatively ineligible without a firm birth year and a clearly dated material breakout by 26.
early_history_summary: Started in Google communications/public affairs, moved to Facebook during early scaling (hundreds of employees, tens of millions of users), worked people/culture and mobile product initiatives, then operations leadership at Quip (sold to Salesforce), Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, Lambda School COO, and founded Glue Club / leadership community work.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources (father reportedly advised against a risky Facebook internal move).
evidence_summary: Wikipedia currently resolves to an unrelated early-20th-century golfer. The Facebook/Google operator Molly Graham is well covered in interviews but lacks a reliably sourced birth year for age-at-milestone verification. Early FB employment is notable but not coded as a dated breakout without firm ages.

name: Terri Burns
milestone_by_age_26: In October 2020, at age 26, promoted to investing partner at GV (Google Ventures)—the firm's youngest partner and first Black woman partner—after joining as principal in 2017.
early_history_summary: Born February 22, 1994 and raised in California; graduated NYU Courant Institute with a CS bachelor's in 2016. Worked as front-end engineer at Venmo and associate product manager at Twitter, then joined GV as principal in 2017 before partner promotion in 2020.
family_context_summary: Raised in California; detailed family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: NYU Courant, Twitter APM, GV, product-to-VC path
evidence_summary: Burns combined CS training and product roles at Venmo/Twitter with mentorship from GV partners, becoming principal at 23 and partner at 26. Domain exposure from building consumer products and investing in Gen-Z startups (e.g., HAGS seed) supported the promotion. Family domain advantages are undocumented; pipeline was institutional (NYU, SF/NY tech, GV).
starting_point: Born February 22, 1994; raised in California; computer science graduate of NYU Courant (2016).
current_position: Founder and general partner of Type Capital (early-stage VC); previously partner at GV; Forbes 30 Under 30; youngest NYU trustee as of 2021.

trajectory.event: Graduated NYU Courant with a bachelor's in computer science; joined Twitter as associate product manager after Venmo engineering.
Joined GV (Google Ventures) as a principal on the investing team.
Promoted to investing partner at GV—youngest partner and first Black woman partner at the firm.
Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 and became the youngest member of NYU's board of trustees.
Launched Type Capital as founder/GP after leaving GV.

name: Barbara Liskov
milestone_by_age_26: No material research milestone by age 26 found. Earned a UC Berkeley BA in mathematics in 1961 at age 21, worked as a programmer at MITRE and Harvard, and received a Stanford CS PhD in March 1968 at age 28. Landmark CLU, Argus, and Liskov substitution principle work and the Turing Award came decades later.
early_history_summary: Born Barbara Jane Huberman in Los Angeles on November 7, 1939; eldest of four. Berkeley math BA (1961), early programming jobs, then Stanford PhD under John McCarthy on chess endgame programs (1968). Later MIT Institute Professor and Turing Award laureate (2008).
family_context_summary: Daughter of Jane (née Dickhoff) and Moses Huberman; Jewish family background noted in secondary sources. Detailed early finances not fully documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as computer-science domain experts in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Liskov is a tier-1 CS pioneer (abstract data types, CLU, LSP, Byzantine fault tolerance) and 2008 Turing Award winner, but her PhD and foundational systems research are after age 26. Early programming jobs and a Berkeley BA by 21 do not meet the material milestone bar used here.
